summary: The root نعق (naʿaqa) primarily means to cry out or shout. It can describe a shepherd calling his flock or, metaphorically, inciting people to conflict or discord.
lane: 1 نَعَقَ بِهِمْ إِلَى الفِتْنَةٍ ذ He hallooed them on to fight, etc.: see 10 in art. عو .

headwords.def: نَعَقَ بِهِمْ إِلَى الفِتْنَةٍ He hallooed them on to fight, etc.: see 10 in art. عو.
One who drives away the beasts, and cries out after them. (TA in art. زعق.)

headword_note: Lane organises by verb form and principal noun, not by every inflected form. A word with no headword entry falls back to the root meaning; nothing is inferred.
